affectedCopies: Trip is the single source of truth for a captured drive; no other model stores drive geometry or distance.
MileageRate is the single source of truth for reimbursement pricing; ExpenseItem stores the resulting money, never the rate logic.
ExpenseClaim / ExpenseItem remain the canonical reimbursement spine — mileage monetises ONTO them rather than opening a parallel reimbursement path.
DriverLocationConsent is the single source of truth for whether background capture is permitted for a driver; capture code must read it, never infer consent.
No existing row is copied, rewritten, or deleted by this change.

migration.name: 20260822100000_add_mileage_absorption_substrate
migration.backfill: None required. The migration is purely additive — new enums, tables, indexes and foreign keys only; no existing column is altered or dropped, so it applies cleanly against any existing data state. Rollback is a drop of the new tables and enums; no existing data depends on them.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: Trip carries precise personal location data and is therefore consent-gated: a row may only be created for a driver holding a granted DriverLocationConsent. DriverLocationConsent.retentionDays DECLARES the geometry retention bound; the field-level minimisation job that enforces it is a named follow-up and is NOT shipped in this substrate change. The row itself is never row-purged — a trip that priced a reimbursement is accounting evidence — so the disposition is domain-lifecycle-managed and minimisation must clear geometry columns rather than delete rows. Rows leave service through the RecordLifecycle convention (lifecycle/lifecycleAt/lifecycleReason), never by silent deletion, so a reimbursement already claimed stays auditable after the underlying geometry is aged out.

fields.reason: startLatitude/startLongitude/endLatitude/endLongitude are precise personal location data about an identified employee. They exist to compute distance and to evaluate commute-exclusion against WorkLocation coordinates, and for no other purpose. Trips classified personal must not expose geometry beyond the device — only distance is required off-device.

reimbursableAmount is derived from distanceMeters and the MileageRate in force on startedAt. It is never edited in place independently of its rate, so a reimbursement can always be re-derived and audited against the rate that priced it.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: Consent records are retained after revocation rather than deleted — the history of who consented, when, under which policy version, and when they revoked is itself the audit evidence. Revocation stops capture; it does not erase the record that consent once existed.

fields.reason: consentStatus and grantedAt/revokedAt are the enforcement input for background location capture. policyVersion pins which disclosure the driver actually agreed to, so a changed policy requires fresh consent rather than inheriting the old grant.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: Vehicles leave service through the RecordLifecycle convention so historical trips keep resolving their vehicle. A company-owned vehicle points at its FixedAsset row so depreciation and mileage share one asset identity rather than duplicating it.

Rates are effective-dated and never edited in place: a rate change closes the current row via effectiveTo and opens a new row. This keeps every already-priced trip reproducible at the rate in force on the day it was driven.
Rules leave service through the RecordLifecycle convention. Trips retain classificationRuleId after a rule is retired so an operator can always see which rule classified a historical trip.
